The International Telecommunications Union (ITU), a UN agency, confirmed on April 22, 2020, that 5G broadband is not responsible for the spread of COVID-19. [1] A spokesperson for ITU stated that the theory linking 5G and COVID-19 is "a hoax that has no technical basis" and that "the coronavirus is not being spread by radio waves." [1] The World Health Organization (WHO) and the US Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) have also stated that viruses cannot travel via radio waves or mobile networks, and that COVID-19 is appearing in countries without advanced wireless systems. [2] [3] [4] The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) notes that exposure to intense non-ionizing radiation can cause tissue damage due to heat, but this is uncommon and mainly a workplace concern. [5] Experts emphasize that 5G technology uses non-ionizing radiation, which does not damage DNA, and there is no scientific basis for the theory that 5G might compromise the immune system. [2] [5] [6] Despite the COVID-19 pandemic starting during the deployment of 5G technology, the two are not connected, and there is indisputable evidence that COVID-19 is a viral disease. [5] Some conspiracy theories suggested that 5G was first tested in Wuhan, China, the city linked to the first cases of COVID-19, but 5G technology was not fully deployed in Wuhan as of 2020. [7] [5]
